1.why: The UI is clean and static across all steps with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions and the active step in the progress bar stand out clearly via dark teal buttons and highlighting, though the persistent Logs panel competes for attention.

3.why: Needed fields, buttons, and the next action are immediately visible on each focused single-purpose screen.

4.why: A visible 5-step progress indicator and short per-screen instructions mean the user does not have to remember rules or the overall sequence.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill affordances, or “remember me” options appear on the password or sign-in screens.

6.why: The flow shows no saved credentials, familiar account markers, or previously used items the user could recognize.

7.why: All instructional text is short, plain-language, and easy to read on every step.

8.why: No error messages or validation failures are shown in the provided screenshots, so problem-and-fix feedback cannot be verified.

9.why: Password rules are stated and codes appear in Logs, but input fields themselves lack inline examples or format placeholders.

10.why: Only password entry and a typed MFA code are offered; no choice of password, code, or face login is presented.

11.why: Each screen presents essentially one decision or action, never a large set of simultaneous choices.

12.why: Status banners after every action explicitly state the outcome (code verified, password saved, signed in, privacy accepted).

13.why: Contextual guidance banners and a persistent Need help? link supply tips for each new step.

14.why: Users can resend a recovery code and re-enter fields freely; the design allows trying again without penalty.

15.why: Layout, progress bar, button style, help link, and Logs panel remain consistent across all seven steps, supporting learning over time.
